name: Remove All Primes
html:
Dear reader, welcome back to another interesting question called REMOVE ALL PRIMES. So, we hope you have studied ArrayList and understood how you can work with them.

Important Links : Problem link, Solution video

Problem Discussion :

This question is based on ArrayList. It states that you have to remove all prime numbers from an ArrayList. Please look at the diagram given below to understand the problem completely.

In the diagram above, there is an ArrayList with both prime as well as non-prime numbers. We have to remove all the prime numbers from this ArrayList. Before we move to the solution, we want you to think about the problem first (This problem looks easy but it is a tricky question). So, have you thought of something? Let"s start our discussion and then you can see whatever you thought was right or can you learn something new( because we are either right or we learn something).

Approach :
  1. Deciding from where to move:
    Dear reader, did you think about the solution? Well, the procedure is not that complex. We just have to traverse the ArrayList and check for all the prime numbers and remove them.
    However, if we start from the front of the arraylist and reach its rear end, this method is not going to produce the desired output. Can you think of why? Have a look at the diagram shown below: See, when you remove the first encountered prime number i.e. 13, the internal shifting of the elements take place and now the next element i.e. 11 has come to index 2 which is also a prime number but, if you look at the code carefully, we simply increment the value of "i" variable so it became 3. This means that in the next iteration we will check whether the element at index 3 is prime or not, but we had a prime number at index 2 that we have already missed. This causes a problem and due to this, all the prime numbers might not get removed from the ArrayList. So, how can we solve this issue? This issue can be solved by starting the iteration from the back of the ArrayList. How? Think !!!!!!
    When we iterate the ArrayList in the reverse direction we will not encounter this issue as the index of the previous elements does not change when we remove a prime element. Have a look at the diagram given below: The "i" variable started from index 10. At index 10 it found 4 which is not a prime number. So, it moved backward at index 9 where it found 7 which is a prime number. So, 7got removed and 4 took the place of it and the index of 3 did not change. So, next time when "i" will be decremented and it checks for index 8 and finds out that the value is 3 which is also prime, 3 will also get removed. If you have any doubts regarding this concept, you may watch the solution video. Watch video
  2. Traversing and Removing Primes:
    Now, since we know that we have to traverse the Arraylist in the backward direction we know the entire procedure. We have to traverse the array and check whether a number is a prime number or not. If it is a prime number, we will remove it. If you have any doubts regarding the concept of a prime number and how to check whether a number is prime or not you may refer to the prime number solution video to clear all your doubts. We recommend you solve this problem first, by clicking here so that you revise the concept in depth by yourself. The internal shifting of the elements will not be done by us. The ArrayList takes care of that itself. You may watch the solution video so that the entire procedure is clear to you. The code for the problem is given below: Watch video
Pseudo Code:
  1. Declare a variable "i" and keep it at the end of ArrayList i.e. the index at which it has its last value. Also, write the function for checking whether a number is prime or not.
  2. Iterate through the ArrayList by decrementing the "i" variable and keep on removing the prime numbers by checking the numbers with the help of your created function.

Think about why we are starting from the back (rear) of the array list and not from the front!!!!!

import java.io.*; import java.util.*; public class Main { public static void solution(ArrayList< Integer> al){ for(int i =a1.size(); i>=0; i--){ if(isPrime(al.get(i))){ al.remove(i); } } } public static boolean isPrime(int n){ for(int i = 2; i * i <= n; i++){ if(n % i == 0){ return false; } } return true; } public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); int n = scn.nextInt(); ArrayList< Integer> al = new ArrayList< >(); for(int i = 0 ; i < n; i++){ al.add(scn.nextInt()); } solution(al); System.out.println(al); } }
java; true";

If you faced any difficulty understanding the code you can refer to the Solution video.

Watch video Analysis Time Complexity :

The time complexity for the above procedure is O(n2). Why? Think about it?

You might think that the time complexity should be O(n) as we are just traversing the Arraylist and removing the prime numbers but, you should not forget about the internal shifting of the elements, although it is not performed by us, it is still happening and we should consider it as well.

SPACE COMPLEXITY :

The space complexity of the procedure is O(1) as we have not used any extra space.

So dear reader, we hope that you have understood the problem completely. If you have any doubts you can check out the complete solution video for clearing all your doubts.

Watch video Suggestions:

Here are some suggestions from our side that you don"t want to miss:

  1. So, first of all, did you enjoy this question? This is a very important question if you ask us, not because it came up in many interviews, but, it tells us the importance of little things in programming. Who thought that just traversing a list in reverse order would make such a difference, right?
  2. Well, let"s think about something that we have not talked about in this question. You are requested to think upon it and try to find it out. We are removing the prime numbers from an Arraylist and we said that due to the internal shifting of the elements, the time complexity of this method is O(n2). But, what if the numbers given in this list are very-very large. Even if you take the optimized way to find whether a number is prime or not, if the square root of the numbers is also in the hundreds or thousands then it will take time to compute whether it is prime or not. What will happen to the time complexity of this solution then? Try to find this out. Happy coding!!!!
